venue: Oriole Park at Camden Yards, Baltimore, MD. CONFIRMED as the Baltimore Orioles' current and only home ballpark for the 2026 season. The name is CURRENT and UNCHANGED: Ballparks of Baseball's Facts & Figures list '-Former Name(s): None' and '-Naming Rights: None' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/camden-yards/); MLB.com's own club pages are still titled 'Oriole Park at Camden Yards' in 2026-dated content (https://www.mlb.com/orioles/ballpark, https://www.mlb.com/orioles/ballpark/ground-rules); RateYourSeats titles every page 'Oriole Park at Camden Yards' under the slug 'oriole-park'. NO stadium naming-rights deal and NO field naming-rights deal was found for 2026 - this park is not a Daikin/Rate Field-style rename case, and unlike Dodger Stadium there is no separate field sponsor. Sponsor names DO attach to features inside the park (T. Rowe Price sign above the videoboard, Coors Light Center Field Roof Deck, Pepsi Picnic Perch, All-Star Cafe) - none of these renames the venue or the field. The park DID change physically for 2026: a $400M+ project begun after the 2025 season added a new centre-field videoboard ~2.5x larger, a right-field wall display, 1,125 feet of new ribbon board, and a NEW premium club behind home plate for ~380 patrons with 'a private entrance, and elevated food and beverage offerings' (https://ballparkdigest.com/2025/06/18/oriole-park-renovations-unveiled-for-2026/). MLB.com adds: 'In January 2025, the Maryland Board of Public Works approved $135 million in bond financing for Camden Yards that went toward a new sound system, a large center-field video board and other visual upgrades. Those features were installed ahead of the '26 season.' (https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/camden-yards-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more). STALE-SOURCE WARNING: any Camden Yards seating chart, capacity figure or club-level section list predating the 2025-26 renovation is STALE - in particular the Club Level sections 232-240 directly behind home plate that older charts show are NOT present in the 2026 RateYourSeats section index, and the new 'Premium Club' (sections C31-C43) occupies the behind-the-plate position instead. Ballparks of Baseball's 45,971 capacity is the 2011-renovation figure and is stale.
concert_only_sections: 'Premium Club' - a ZONE LINK on the RateYourSeats section index (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections) with NO per-section pages. It is a BASEBALL premium seating area, not a concert-floor area, but its constituent section IDs are not enumerated as individual links in the section index, so they are recorded here rather than in `sections`. Zone page https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/premium-club states verbatim: 'A brand new premium seating area debuting Opening Day 2026', 'Located directly behind home plate in Sections C31-C43', positioned 'slightly below the Club Level', 'Premium Club seats are extremely limited at Camden Yards, with only a small number of seats available', with 'Inclusive food and beverage package', 'Private stadium entrance', 'Access to a new indoor club with floor-to-ceiling glass', 'Dining tables and multiple bars', 'Private restrooms'. SO: the letter-prefixed IDs C31, C33, C35, C37, C39, C41, C43 (or C31 through C43 inclusive - the page gives only the range, not the members) exist as 2026 ticketed baseball sections but are NOT individually indexed. DO NOT invent the members of this range.

'Standing Room Only' - a ZONE LINK on the RateYourSeats section index (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections) with NO per-section pages and NO section identifiers. The linked page https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/standing-room-only returned no statement of where SRO areas are located at Oriole Park. Location: UNKNOWN.
NO concert-floor sections were found for Oriole Park at Camden Yards on the RateYourSeats section index. The index contains no 'Field Sections' / floor-seating group.
capacity: CONFLICTING FIGURES - three sources, three numbers, and the discrepancy is material because the 2025-26 renovation changed the seat count. (1) Wikipedia infobox capacity history: '48,876' (1992-2010) reduced by the 2011 renovation - 'The renovation reduced Oriole Park's capacity from 48,876 to 45,971'; then 44,487 for 2022-2025; and '2026-present' listed as 42,455 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oriole_Park_at_Camden_Yards). (2) MLB.com Camden Yards guide: capacity '44,970' (https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/camden-yards-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more). (3) Ballparks of Baseball Facts & Figures: '-Capacity: 45,971' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/camden-yards/) - this is the 2011-renovation figure and is STALE. RECOMMENDED for 2026: 42,455 (the only figure explicitly scoped to '2026-present'), with 44,970 recorded as the club-published alternative. DO NOT use 45,971.

orientation.batter_faces: Home plate faces south-southwest; the batter looks out toward centre field to the north-northeast.
orientation.verbatim: 'Camden Yards has a north-northeast-facing orientation (roughly 30 degrees), meaning home plate faces south-southwest and center field points to the north-northeast.' Same page: 'The sun in Baltimore travels through the southern sky, reaching its highest point due south at midday and then tracking toward the southwest through the afternoon.'
orientation.consistency_check: Consistent with the RateYourSeats shade page, which says the THIRD BASE side shades first and warns 'Completely avoid sections 1-8 in the Right Field corner if you want to stay out of the sun' because they get 'direct sun exposure ... during late afternoon and evening games' - i.e. the first-base/right-field side is the sun side and the third-base side is the shade side, which is what a NNE-facing bowl produces.
orientation.confidence: medium-high (one explicit compass statement, cross-checked against two independent shade descriptions)

numbering_direction.summary: SECTION NUMBERS INCREASE FROM THE RIGHT-FIELD / FIRST-BASE SIDE TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE / LEFT-FIELD SIDE - i.e. they INCREASE TOWARD THIRD BASE. LOW numbers = right-field corner and the first-base side. MIDDLE numbers = behind home plate. HIGH numbers = third base, then left field, then (continuing around past the bullpens) the bleachers in centre / right-centre field. The bowl SWEEPS CONTINUOUSLY ONE WAY: right-field corner (1 / 4) -> first base (20-26) -> home plate (33-39) -> third base (48-52) -> left field (56-82) -> left-centre bullpens (84-86) -> bleachers (90-98). EVERY series at the park runs this same direction: lower bowl 1-98, Club Level 204-288, Upper Level 306-388.
numbering_direction.parity_signature_check: NO - Oriole Park does NOT use the NL West outward-from-home-plate-by-parity scheme. Parity at Camden Yards encodes DEPTH, NOT DIRECTION. In the lower bowl the EVEN sections are the front (field-level) sections and the ODD sections are the rear (terrace-level) sections directly behind them, both running the SAME low-to-high direction and roughly aligned with each other (e.g. even 34 and odd 33-39 are all behind home plate; even 24 and odd 23 are both near the Orioles dugout). The Stadium Insiders states this plainly: 'even sections are down the steps, and the odd sections are up the steps' (https://thestadiuminsiders.com/stadium_guides/baltimore-orioles/ticketing-seating-premium/), and RateYourSeats' Field Level page says Field Level 'include[s] even-numbered sections below 100 (e.g., 20, 40, etc.)' while Section 1 is described as 'an odd-numbered lower level section on the Terrace Level'. NO statement of the form 'sections 111-115 on the first base side and 112-116 on the third base side' was found anywhere for this park. The Club Level and Upper Level are ALL-EVEN series (the single odd entry, 381, is an anomaly - see `uncertain`), which is a numbering-stride quirk, not a parity split.
numbering_direction.anchor_right_field: (a) RateYourSeats Section 1: 'Section 1 is an odd-numbered lower level section on the Terrace Level, positioned in right field' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections/1). (b) RateYourSeats Terrace Level zone page: 'Sections 1-9 (right field)' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/terrace-level). (c) RateYourSeats shade page: 'Completely avoid sections 1-8 in the Right Field corner if you want to stay out of the sun' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats). (d) The Stadium Insiders lists 'Front field outfield (even sections 4-18, 56-82)' - the 4-18 half being the right-field half.
numbering_direction.anchor_home_plate: (a) RateYourSeats Section 34: 'Desirable view from behind home plate' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections/34). (b) RateYourSeats Terrace Level zone page: sections '33-39' are 'behind home plate' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/terrace-level). (c) RateYourSeats Upper Level zone page: 'Sections 330-342 offer strong views of the entire field from behind home plate' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/upper-level). (d) HARD FACT, official Orioles accessibility guide: 'Elevators are available behind home plate (near Section 36) and in left field (behind Section 78).' (https://www.mlb.com/orioles/ballpark/disability-access-guide)
numbering_direction.anchor_left_field: (a) HARD FACT, official Orioles accessibility guide: 'Elevators are available behind home plate (near Section 36) and in left field (behind Section 78).' (https://www.mlb.com/orioles/ballpark/disability-access-guide) - Section 78 is IN LEFT FIELD. (b) The Stadium Insiders: 'Front field outfield (even sections 4-18, 56-82)' - the 56-82 half being the left-field half; and 'Bird Bath (sections 84-86)' adjacent to the left-centre bullpens. (c) RateYourSeats Field Level page: 'Fans interested in watching pitchers warm up should look toward Section 86, where the team bullpens are located' - and MLB.com ground rules refer to 'the left-center bullpens', placing Section 86 in left-centre field.
numbering_direction.anchor_dugout_cross_check: RateYourSeats Field Level zone page: 'Orioles Dugout: Located behind Sections 22, 24, and 26' and 'Visitor Dugout: Located behind Sections 48, 50, and 52' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/field-level). Ballparks of Baseball independently states '-Home Dugout: First Base'. Therefore 22-26 (LOW) = first base and 48-52 (HIGH) = third base, which fixes the direction independently of the outfield anchors. RateYourSeats Section 50 confirms: 'These seats are located behind the visitor dugout' and 'Rows 1-10 are recommended for visiting team fans'.
numbering_direction.club_level_direction: RateYourSeats Club Level zone page: 'Sections 204-240 along the first base side' and 'Sections 242-280 along the third base side' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/club-level) - same low-to-high, first-base-to-third-base direction. Corroborated by the shade page: 'Sections 242-264 will be entirely shaded by the middle innings' (the third-base/shade side).
numbering_direction.confidence: HIGH. Five independent anchor types agree (right-field section page, terrace zone page, shade page, official Orioles elevator statement, dugout statements + Ballparks of Baseball home-dugout side). No source contradicts the direction.

dugouts.cross_check: Geometry is self-consistent: the low-numbered dugout (22-26) is on the same side as the low-numbered right-field corner (1-8), and the high-numbered dugout (48-52) is on the same side as left field (Section 78, per the official Orioles elevator statement). No source inverts this.

bullpens: BOTH bullpens are beyond the outfield wall in LEFT-CENTRE FIELD, in a stacked two-tier arrangement. Wikipedia: the bullpens occupy left-center field behind the playing area, and their 'unique two-tiered design was a first in major league parks', with a picnic area featuring orange umbrellas positioned above them (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oriole_Park_at_Camden_Yards). MLB.com ground rules refer to lowering the wall 'to 6 feet, 11 inches closer to the left-center bullpens' (https://www.mlb.com/orioles/ballpark/ground-rules). The adjacent seating is Section 86: RateYourSeats Field Level page - 'Fans interested in watching pitchers warm up should look toward Section 86, where the team bullpens are located'; the Section 86 page adds that the Orioles bullpen occupies the first ten rows of the view and visiting pitchers warm up in rows 12 and above, and a fan review says 'Best thing about these seats is being able to watch the bullpen' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections/86). The Stadium Insiders names sections 84-86 the 'Bird Bath'. NOTE: RateYourSeats' phrasing about which bullpen is 'first ten rows' vs 'rows 12 and above' is ambiguous as to home/visitor assignment within the two tiers - no source states which tier is the Orioles' - so that detail is UNKNOWN.

accessibility.accessible_row_evidence: RateYourSeats Section 336 (Upper Level): 'Rows in Section 336 are labeled 1-5, 9-25' with wheelchair seating between rows 5 and 9 - i.e. the gap where rows 6-8 would be is the wheelchair platform. This row-gap pattern is the observable accessible-row convention at Oriole Park; the club publishes no row-label convention of its own.

row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERS at every tier, per RateYourSeats. There is one non-numeric row label in wide use: 'EAL', which marks the section's entrance row. LOWER BOWL - FIELD LEVEL (even): 'Rows in Section 20 are labeled 1-27, EAL'; 'Rows in Section 24 are labeled 1-24, EAL'; 'Rows in Section 30 are labeled 1-29, EAL'; 'Rows in Section 34 are labeled 1-29, EAL'; 'Rows in Section 50 are labeled 1-24, EAL'; 'Rows in Section 86 are labeled 1-13' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row EAL.' LOWER BOWL - TERRACE LEVEL (odd): 'Rows in Section 1 are labeled 1-17' (no EAL shown on this page). BLEACHERS: 'Rows in Section 96 are labeled 1-22, EAL'; 'Rows in Section 98 are labeled 1-15, EAL'. CLUB LEVEL: short sections - 'Rows in Section 246 are labeled 1-9'; 'Rows in Section 230 are labeled 1-9', with an entrance located at Row 9. 'Rows 8 and above are under cover.' UPPER LEVEL: 'Rows in Section 336 are labeled 1-5, 9-25' (rows 6-8 absent; wheelchair seating sits between rows 5 and 9); 'Rows in Section 381 are labeled 8-25' (starts at 8, not 1). 'Rows 15 and above in the upper deck' are covered. ACCESSIBLE-ROW CONVENTION: no lettered accessible-row label was found; instead accessible positions appear as a NUMBERED GAP in the row sequence (Section 336: 1-5, 9-25). CONFLICTING SOURCE: Ballpark E-Guides describes LETTERED rows at Camden Yards - row designations beginning with 'AA' as the front row, then 'A-CCC', and says 'Row AA' is 'not quite near the field' - and puts upper-level rows at 'approximately Row 25'. This directly contradicts RateYourSeats' all-numeric row labels for every section checked. Recorded in `uncertain`; NOT reconciled. Sources: https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections/1 , /20, /24, /30, /34, /50, /86, /96, /98, /230, /246, /336, /381 ; https://ballparkeguides.com/camden-yards-seating-tips/
seat1_side_verbatim: RATEYOURSEATS, VERBATIM, identical on every Oriole Park section page checked: "When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the right". NOTE THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MORE COMMON RATEYOURSEATS BOILERPLATE ('lower number seats are on the left') used at other parks in this project - do not carry that phrasing over. VERIFIED VERBATIM on these Oriole Park section pages, deliberately spread across the whole bowl: 1 (right field, Terrace), 20 (Field Level, right-field/first-base half), 24 (behind the Orioles dugout, FIRST BASE side), 30 (Field Level, infield), 34 (BEHIND HOME PLATE), 50 (behind the visitor dugout, THIRD BASE side), 86 (LEFT-CENTRE field, at the bullpens), 96 and 98 (bleachers), 230 and 246 (Club Level), 336 and 381 (Upper Level). So RateYourSeats gives the SAME 'on the right' answer on the first-base side, behind the plate, on the third-base side, in left-centre and in the outfield bleachers - it treats seat numbering as running uniformly right-to-left as the fan faces the field, everywhere in the park. PER-SECTION CORROBORATION (beats boilerplate): the Section 86 page adds an independent, section-specific sentence - 'Higher number seats are closer to the left side of Section 86' - which AGREES with the park-wide sentence. INDEPENDENT SECOND SOURCE, AGREES: Ballpark E-Guides states "Facing the field, Seat 1 is always on your right." (https://ballparkeguides.com/camden-yards-seating-tips/). NO DISAGREEMENT FOUND between the two sources at Oriole Park. CAVEAT: 'lower number seats are on the right' as the fan faces the field means seat 1 is toward THIRD BASE on the first-base side and toward the RIGHT-FIELD CORNER on the third-base side - i.e. under this rule seat 1 is NOT uniformly the home-plate-nearest seat. No official Orioles source states a seat-numbering rule at all, so this rule rests entirely on RateYourSeats plus Ballpark E-Guides. Sources: https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections/1 , /20, /24, /30, /34, /50, /86, /96, /98, /230, /246, /336, /381 ; https://ballparkeguides.com/camden-yards-seating-tips/
known_obstructions: NETTING: No per-section netting/screening note is published by RateYourSeats for Oriole Park - sections 20, 30 and 34 were checked explicitly and NONE carries the 'Front of sections ... are behind the netting or fencing' note that the site prints at other parks. Per-section netting extent is therefore UNKNOWN from the ticketing source. The only netting statement found is MLB.com's 2019 announcement (dated 29 August 2019), which says the netting extends "down the foul lines and nearly to the foul poles at each corner of Oriole Park at Camden Yards", installed before the 5 September 2019 game (https://www.mlb.com/news/orioles-extending-ballpark-s-protective-netting). Treat this as pole-to-pole-adjacent coverage of the lower bowl foul territory; no section numbers are given, and no 2026 re-confirmation was found. SUN EXPOSURE (functional obstruction): 'Completely avoid sections 1-8 in the Right Field corner if you want to stay out of the sun'; 'Except for sections 1-7, all Terrace Level seats are shaded for afternoon games'; covered areas are 'Terrace sections except 1-7 and 33-39', 'Rows 15 and above in the upper deck', and 'Any 200-level club section' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats). RateYourSeats Section 1 notes it 'may be more exposed to the elements' with less overhead coverage than other Terrace sections. VIDEOBOARD SIGHTLINES: Ballpark E-Guides reports (paraphrased on the page, not a clean quote) that bleacher seating cannot see the Jumbotron 'unless you sit in Section 98 and crane your neck'. VIEW QUALITY: RateYourSeats Section 86 fan review - the reviewer praised the bullpen view but 'cautioned that overall viewing angles of gameplay are suboptimal'. OUTFIELD WALL (2025 change, affects sightlines and ground rules): MLB.com ground rules - 'Moving the wall in as much as 26 feet near the bullpen and 13 feet closer to the left field corner' and 'Lowering the previous 13-foot wall to 8 feet near the left field foul pole and to 6 feet, 11 inches closer to the left-center bullpens.' No source lists pole, railing or glass-partition obstructions at Oriole Park. Anything beyond the above is UNKNOWN.
uncertain: BLEACHERS (90-98) LOCATION - THREE-WAY CONFLICT, and it matters because it is the far end of the numbering sweep. (a) RateYourSeats Bleachers zone page and the Section 96 and 98 pages all say 'Located in Sections 90-98 below the main scoreboard in RIGHT-CENTER field' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/bleachers). (b) Wikipedia: 'Bleacher sections (90-98) line Eutaw Street, a pedestrian thoroughfare between the stadium and the Baltimore & Ohio Warehouse at Camden Yards' - i.e. BEYOND RIGHT FIELD (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oriole_Park_at_Camden_Yards). (c) The Stadium Insiders: 'Center field bleachers (sections 90-98)' - CENTRE FIELD. All three place them somewhere in the centre-to-right-centre arc, but they do not agree more precisely. NOTE this does NOT threaten the numbering direction, which is fixed independently by five other anchors: the sweep runs right field (1) -> first base -> home plate -> third base -> left field (78) -> left-centre bullpens (86) -> and then CONTINUES past centre to the bleachers (90-98). Under that reading, 98 ends up back near right-centre, adjacent-but-not-contiguous to 1 across the Eutaw Street / flag court gap - which reconciles (a), (b) and (c). Recorded rather than resolved.
CAPACITY - THREE FIGURES: Wikipedia 42,455 ('2026-present'), MLB.com 44,970, Ballparks of Baseball 45,971 (stale 2011-renovation figure). See `capacity`.

MISSING CLUB-LEVEL SECTIONS 232, 234, 236, 238, 240 (and 224, 266). RateYourSeats' Club Level zone page still describes the tier as 'Sections 204-240 along the first base side', but the 2026 section index contains no link for any of 232-240, and https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections/232 does not resolve to a section page. The obvious inference is that the new 2026 Premium Club ('Sections C31-C43', 'directly behind home plate', 'slightly below the Club Level') took over that behind-the-plate stretch - BUT NO SOURCE STATES THIS. Do not assert it. 224 and 266 are also absent with no explanation.

PREMIUM CLUB SECTION IDs C31-C43 are given only as a RANGE. Whether the members are C31, C33, C35, C37, C39, C41, C43 (odd stride, matching the letter-block convention) or every integer C31..C43 is NOT stated. Do not enumerate them.

SECTION 381 is the ONLY odd-numbered section in an otherwise all-even 300 series, and its rows start at 8 ('Rows in Section 381 are labeled 8-25') rather than 1. No source explains what it is. It IS present in the index (confirmed on a second, independent read of the index page).

SECTION-INDEX COUNT. Two independent reads of https://www.rateyourseats.com/oriole-park/seating/sections returned an IDENTICAL membership list (163 numbered sections plus the 'Premium Club' and 'Standing Room Only' zone links), and a third targeted read confirmed the absence of 2, 21, 25, 41, 51, 57, 63, 88, 224, 232, 240, 266, 302 and 314 and the presence of 381. However that third read reported a total of '155 total section links' and named Section 87 as the highest in the 1-99 series, which is inconsistent with sections 90-98 having live pages (96 and 98 were fetched successfully). Treat the 163-member list in `sections` as the best available, and re-verify the index directly before generating output.

ROW LABELS - LETTERS vs NUMBERS. RateYourSeats reports all-NUMERIC rows (plus the 'EAL' entrance row) on every section page checked. Ballpark E-Guides describes LETTERED rows beginning 'AA' then 'A-CCC' and says 'Row AA' is 'not quite near the field'. These cannot both be current. RateYourSeats is the ticketing-side source and is preferred, but the disagreement is unresolved.

SEAT-1 RULE rests on RateYourSeats' park-wide sentence plus one Ballpark E-Guides sentence; NO official Orioles source states a seat-numbering rule. The two agree, and one per-section sentence (Section 86: 'Higher number seats are closer to the left side of Section 86') corroborates. Still, given that this same boilerplate has been correct on one half of the ballpark and wrong on the other at two parks in this project, spot-check at least one third-base-side and one left-field section against seat-view photos before publishing seat-1 statements.

NETTING EXTENT for 2026 is not confirmed by any current source; the only statement is the 2019 MLB.com announcement of netting 'nearly to the foul poles'. No per-section netting note exists on RateYourSeats for this park.

GATE LETTERS CONFLICT: the Orioles accessibility guide names 'Gate G' for the Family Wellness Rooms and 'Gate A' / 'Gate D' for drop-off and mobility needs; the MLB.com A-to-Z guide lists standard gates as 'A, D, & H' and Accessibility/Medical & Family gates as 'C, D, & H'. Gate G does not appear in the A-to-Z list.

ACCESSIBLE SEATING SECTIONS: the club publishes no section list ('Accessible seats are located throughout Oriole Park in virtually all ticket categories'). Per-section accessible locations are UNKNOWN except the Section 336 row-gap evidence.
STANDING ROOM ONLY locations are UNKNOWN - the zone page states nothing.
BULLPEN TIER ASSIGNMENT (which of the two stacked left-centre bullpens is the Orioles') is UNKNOWN; RateYourSeats' 'first ten rows' / 'rows 12 and above' phrasing on the Section 86 page is ambiguous.
COORS LIGHT CENTER FIELD ROOF DECK: no section identifiers stated.
ORIENTATION rests on a single explicit compass statement (theshadium.com, 'roughly 30 degrees'). It is consistent with two independent shade descriptions but has no official corroboration.
